mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not exceed the baseline mean during periods of low FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive 20-day returns occur despite high unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative or flat returns occur despite housing growth.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production signals economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns do not increase during production growth periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment and employment suggest labor market contradictions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite conflicting labor signals.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate indicates tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur with high FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales indicate strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Returns do not increase with retail sales growth.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth with controlled inflation indicates balanced expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% and CPIAUCSL growth < 3% in 3 months
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite balanced growth.
